svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag and Drop
svg.desc: A static textbook-style learning screen. Select a term in the word bank to highlight that flower part. Hint, Check Answer, and Reset open overlay panels via internal links. No script required.

g.text: complete flower · one carpel shown in section
Match each term to the flower
This screen is a static study board. There is no live dragging.
Use the word-bank tiles or the dashed slots as links:
1. Choose a term. That part lights up on the diagram.
2. Read the caption that appears on the selected part.
3. Open Hint if you need a nudge, or Check Answer for the key.
4. Reset returns you to the unlabeled workspace.
Name the sterile parts (sepal, petal, receptacle) and the fertile parts.
Split the stamen into anther + filament and the pistil into stigma + style + ovary.
Connect those structures to pollination and seed formation.
Anchor navigation only · one highlight at a time · no script
2. A tube grows down the style.
3. Sperm reach ovules in the ovary.
Stamen makes pollen · pistil receives it · ovary becomes fruit
WORD BANK · SELECT A TILE TO PLACE IT ON THE DIAGRAM
tiles look draggable · they navigate by anchor
Tip: stamen = anther + filament. Pistil (carpel) = stigma + style + ovary. Sepals protect the bud; petals advertise to pollinators.
Flower Anatomy Lab · static SVG study board · terms follow a standard introductory botany key
Outer green bract; together they are the calyx.
Male organ: filament plus pollen-bearing anther.
Female organ (carpel): stigma, style, and ovary.
Lobed tip of the stamen that releases pollen.
Stalk that holds the anther into the air stream.
Swollen base holding ovules; becomes the fruit.
Neck of the pistil; the pollen tube grows through it.
Sticky tip that captures arriving pollen grains.
Expanded stem tip where all floral parts attach.
three nudges, then the map of the flower
Outside in: sepal, then petal, then the fertile organs on the receptacle.
Anything gold and dusty is anther. The stalk under it is filament. Both = stamen.
Down the middle: stigma (landing pad), style (tube), ovary (chamber of ovules) = pistil.
Still stuck? Open Check Answer for the completed board, then Reset to practice again.
Because this file cannot score a live drag, the key shows the intended matching. Compare it with the diagram, then Reset to quiz yourself again.
sepal — green flaps under the petals
anther — gold pollen sacs at the tip
filament — slender stalk of the stamen
stigma — sticky lobes at the very top
style — neck between stigma and ovary
receptacle — green cushion on the stem
All slots on the official key
are filled. Use Reset to hide them.
Common mix-ups: anther vs stigma (gold vs pink tip);
sepal vs petal (green vs colored); ovary vs receptacle
All highlights and placed chips are hidden when you
return to the unlabeled board. Word-bank tiles stay
available. This is the same as starting the lab over.
Nothing is stored — this file has no memory, cookies,
or script. Closing this panel is the reset.
